rv.q: Bronagh Lagan's production – at the play's London premiere – is fired with charm.

That built-in affection is fortunate, then, for "Little Women: The Musical," a pleasant but staid revisitation that's too leisurely in locating the heart of the material. But the producers of this unapologetically old-fashioned tuner have secured an appealing, capable cast whose conviction and energy help bolster the mostly unmemorable songs.
If you like your musical theatre ballsy and meaty, you may find all this wholesomeness a little hard to take.
Allan Knee's book is oddly paced and the story arcs lack momentum.
It's painfully obvious they never got to know their title characters very well, either.
